authenticationTransportCorrection.trigger: After the old session expired during QA, sign-in authenticated the test admin but redirected back to login in the local production build.
authenticationTransportCorrection.cause: authOptions chooses secure-cookie names from NODE_ENV; the middleware relied on NextAuth auto-detection from NEXTAUTH_URL. Production HTTP on localhost therefore read the wrong cookie name, and could keep using an older development cookie.
authenticationTransportCorrection.change: Pass secureCookie: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" to getToken, matching the existing authOptions policy. No credential, cookie security flag, session duration, signing secret or role authorization rule changed.
authenticationTransportCorrection.replay: Fresh sign-out/sign-in for manager, staff, cashier and admin succeeded in the final production build. All eight protected integration paths then used the actual new role: manager retained routes; staff/cashier redirected to POS with the matching from parameter.

qaHarnessCorrection.defect: The first custom dev-server attempt shared root .next because Next 14 custom-server preparation reloads configuration and ignores the passed conf. It removed local QA production manifests and caused local 500s.
qaHarnessCorrection.correction: Stopped the owned dev/production processes, moved dev into a disposable source+messages snapshot with the standard CLI and separate localhost cookie host, rebuilt production, then replayed final browser captures and scanner checks. Initial snapshot omission of messages was fixed before successful sign-in. Root Next/TypeScript configuration is unchanged.
qaHarnessCorrection.result: The final dev run exited cleanly and production middleware manifest remained byte-identical. Local QA harness fault, not a product/payment failure; no main merge, external provider operation or customer database affected.
